subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is an academic who developed a theological treatise on punctual tears and the alignment of Shar and Selûne, and has been published by others as a new doctrine, distracting the Avowed from an active murder in Candlekeep.
source_quote: The treatise listed the others. Keep riding west, or shift to another plane, or have someone who can call on the healing that draws a poison clean out of the blood.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is an investigator with expertise in magical detection, currently tracking the murder of a scholar and the theft of a summoning key and sapphire, and has examined a key for magical binding without success.
source_quote: I took custody of the key, set my fingers to the cold iron of it, and let the spell read the object the way an auditor reads an account someone else kept.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a pragmatic investigator who prioritizes identifying the killer over recovering stolen items, and has reconstructed the timeline of the poisoned book and the nature of the poison's activation.
source_quote: A murder is a kind of terrain... you watch where he puts his feet.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is a scholar who delivered a poisoned book as a gift, fears he is being framed for murder, and has revealed the location of the Oak Tree Apothecary as a potential source for poison identification.
source_quote: The Oak Tree Apothecary, he said, between the Sea Warden's Tower and the House of Mechanus, a treehouse grown into the roots of an evergreen oak.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a meticulous scholar who analyzes textual and magical patterns, and has questioned the nature of the summoning magic, the key, and the sapphire, suspecting a deeper connection yet unresolvable.
source_quote: One true sun, light being furthest — and then he'd want to know whether any physical property could slow that light down.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch was a scholar who carried a key bound to a summoning sapphire, feared theft of his key, and was murdered — his key was stolen, and he was killed to sever his possession of it.
source_quote: The stolen sapphire carried a summoning working — it could pull an item to you, but only an item not in anyone's possession. And a dead person, it turns out, possesses nothing.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi is a Candlekeep keeper who retrieved the poisoned book at dinner, after it had been left under the evergreen tree, making them a critical witness in the timeline of the poisoning.
source_quote: The book got picked up by Janussi at dinner. And at the time, it was wrapped.

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris is an Avowed assigned to monitor the investigators, who abandoned his post to attend Grygum’s theological debate, creating an unguarded hour in Candlekeep.
source_quote: Our minder... wanted to attend a debate... Bookwyrm herself unable to politically afford to miss it.

subject: Leuwin
fact: Leuwin is an elderly satyr druid at the Oak Tree Apothecary, known for being absent-minded and keeping a pet squirrel, and is the only person who can definitively identify the poison from the book.
source_quote: A satyr druid named Leuwin, elderly and absent-minded, with a pet squirrel, who could identify the poison from the book definitively.

subject: Avowed
fact: The Avowed are the scholarly guardians of Candlekeep, whose institutional obsession with academic debate and publication has caused them to neglect critical security duties during an active murder investigation.
source_quote: The whole Avowed community wanted, right then and there, to drop everything and debate it in the Grand Hall.

subject: Followers of Kelemvor
fact: The followers of Kelemvor have established through their god's cryptic teachings that the dead possess nothing, and that death is the cleanest method to sever magical possession of an object.
source_quote: An undead can. A dead man can't. The followers of Kelemvor have made that point very clear, repeatedly, through their god's usual incomprehensible cryptic phrasing.

subject: murder of Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch was murdered to sever his possession of a key bound to a summoning sapphire, as only the dead cannot possess items, allowing the key to be retrieved by the sapphire's magic.
source_quote: The cleanest way to free it from his possession was to make him a corpse.

subject: poisoning of the book
fact: The book was poisoned with a substance that activates upon contact with living saliva, turning black after death, and was likely tampered with after Daral left it under the tree but before Janussi retrieved it at dinner.
source_quote: The poison sitting in somebody's room right now wouldn't be black at all. It'd be clear.

subject: theft of the summoning sapphire and key
fact: A sapphire and a key were stolen from Kalan Strongbranch’s safe and locket; the sapphire is the retrieval token for the key, and the key must be separated from its possessor via death to be retrieved.
source_quote: The sapphire isn't decoration: it's the retrieval token, and it has to be the same sapphire both to store and to recall.

subject: Grygum's theological debate
fact: Grygum’s debate on the alignment of Shar and Selûne drew away key personnel including Fembris and Bookwyrm, creating an unguarded hour during which the murder’s evidence could have been moved or planted.
source_quote: A keeper of the keep, leaving his post, to watch the orc argue dragons.

subject: subject": "summoning sapphire
fact: The sapphire is a magical retrieval token for a key, activated only by the caster’s spell, and functions only when the key is no longer in a living person’s possession.
source_quote: Possess the gem and you possess the item, provided you have the magic to call it.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch's key
fact: The key was bound to the summoning sapphire and hidden in a locket around Kalan Strongbranch’s neck; it was stolen after his death, which freed it from his possession and allowed retrieval.
source_quote: The stolen sapphire carried a summoning working — it could pull an item to you, but only an item not in anyone's possession.

subject: poisoned book
fact: The book was poisoned with a latent, non-visible toxin that activates upon contact with living saliva, turning black only after death — it was wrapped when retrieved, suggesting the poison was applied before delivery.
source_quote: Why did it turn dark, but it's not dark on the book? Because it goes black after you die.

subject: unresolved connection between key, sapphire, and killer
fact: A pattern exists linking the stolen key, the summoning sapphire, and the murderer — Daz recognizes it but cannot name the connection, suggesting a hidden magical or personal tie yet unproven.
source_quote: There was a connection sitting in the gem and the stolen key and the murdered man... I reached for it and came up with nothing.

subject: true identity of the poisoner
fact: The poison was likely applied to the book before it was left under the tree — but who had access, motive, and knowledge of the activation condition? The identity remains unknown.
source_quote: Either somebody went into his house, tampered with it, knowing he was gonna give it to them, somebody unwrapped it, tampered with it, and then wrapped it back up.

subject: Oak Tree Apothecary
fact: The Oak Tree Apothecary is a treehouse apothecary located between the Sea Warden's Tower and the House of Mechanus, operated by the absent-minded satyr druid Leuwin, and is the only place where the poison can be definitively identified.
source_quote: A treehouse grown into the roots of an evergreen oak.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a vast, dangerous library and seat of arcane scholarship, where academic rivalries and institutional distraction have allowed a murder to go uninvestigated while scholars debate theology.
source_quote: There is an active murder running through this keep. And nothing says you are an academic institution quite like blowing off everything important to focus on what really matters: new research.

subject: Oval Theater
fact: The Oval Theater is the site of Grygum’s theological debate, where key Avowed have gathered, leaving the library vulnerable to further tampering or concealment of evidence.
source_quote: A disputation in the Oval Theater on his new theology, with half the avowed already in attendance.

subject: Deadwinter's Eve
fact: Deadwinter's Eve is the day when the poisoned book was left under the evergreen tree at 11am, retrieved at dinner, and the scholar was murdered — the critical temporal anchor for the investigation.
source_quote: He'd dropped the book under the evergreen tree, next to the other gifts, around 11am on Deadwinter's Eve.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a drow who can communicate with beasts and was present at the Deadwinter supper where poison was administered; he attempted to analyze the murder weapon but lacked the means to extract its full properties.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is the stealthiest member of the group, who deduced the double-stroke nature of the murder — framing Daral and killing Janussi — and identified A'lai Aivenmore as the prime suspect motivated by ideological ambition.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is an ooze-like entity from Blingdenstone who has learned silence and attempted to grow a nose to detect the poison; it consistently seeks to assist despite its limitations and lack of sensory organs.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is a scholar and poet who gave Janussi the poisoned book, is being framed for the murder, and believes the killer sought to eliminate him as a threat to A'lai Aivenmore's ascension.

subject: A'lai Aivenmore
fact: A'lai Aivenmore is a high-ranking official in Candlekeep who seeks to assume control of the keep; he views Daral's love of fiction and poetry as an ideological threat and is the suspected architect of the double-stroke murder.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was a council member murdered by poison administered through a book; his heart was later removed and hidden in the lead-lined Milil chalice to prevent resurrection or questioning.

subject: Irony
fact: Irony is a junior avowed who served at the Deadwinter supper and claims to always tell the truth; she witnessed the event and noted Janussi's reaction to Alkrist's project and the gift-giving ritual.

subject: Sprig
fact: Sprig is a junior avowed who served food at the Deadwinter supper and acted as the official poison taster; she tasted all dishes before they were served and is a key witness to the absence of food-based poisoning.

subject: Candlekeep Council
fact: The Candlekeep Council is a governing body of scholars and mages responsible for determining the direction of magical knowledge; internal power struggles, particularly between Daral and A'lai, led to the murder as a means of political elimination.

subject: Deadwinter Supper
fact: The Deadwinter Supper was a formal gathering where poison was administered via a book given to Janussi; gift-giving, shared platters, and the presence of the lead-lined Milil chalice created multiple vectors for concealment and misdirection.

subject: Heart Removal and Chalice Concealment
fact: Janussi's heart was removed post-mortem and placed inside the lead-lined Milil chalice to prevent magical resurrection or scrying; this act confirmed the killer had deep knowledge of Candlekeep's magical defenses.

subject: Poison Analysis Attempt
fact: Zalthir and Glabbagool attempted to analyze the poison by having Glabbagool grow a nose; the effort failed but demonstrated the group’s commitment to unconventional investigative methods.

subject: Interview with Irony
fact: Irony provided critical testimony about the supper's dynamics, including Janussi's praise of Alkrist’s project, the Secret Santa gift exchange, and Sprig’s role as poison taster — all of which helped eliminate alternative theories.

subject: The Poisoned Book
fact: The poisoned book was given to Janussi by Daral and contained a slow-acting toxin; it was the primary murder weapon and the focal point of the framing scheme against Daral.

subject: Milil's Lead-Lined Chalice
fact: The ceremonial chalice of Milil, made of lead-lined brass, was used to conceal Janussi’s heart to block magical detection; its use confirmed the killer’s intimate knowledge of Candlekeep’s magical infrastructure.

subject: Blood-Stained Meat Cleaver
fact: Found alongside Janussi’s heart in the chalice, the cleaver suggests ritualistic or symbolic violence; its presence implies the killer intended to send a message beyond mere murder.

subject: Wrapping Paper from Secret Santa
fact: The wrapping paper from Janussi’s gift was found in his office, not at the supper; its absence from the scene suggested the gift exchange was a cover for the poison’s delivery or a distraction.

subject: A'lai's Ascension
fact: The political maneuvering behind A'lai Aivenmore’s bid for leadership remains unresolved; his motive is clear, but his direct involvement and methods of execution require further corroboration.

subject: Glabbagool's Sensory Evolution
fact: Glabbagool’s attempt to grow a nose raises the possibility of evolving new sensory capabilities; whether this leads to future breakthroughs in detection or merely highlights its tragic determination is an open question.

subject: The Identity of the Heart's Extractor
fact: Who removed Janussi’s heart and placed it in the chalice remains unknown; the act requires post-mortem access and surgical precision, pointing to a second operative or a highly skilled killer.

subject: Candlekeep Dining Hall
fact: The southern dining hall is the site of the Deadwinter supper and the later discovery of Janussi’s heart; its layout, statues, and ceremonial objects played key roles in the murder’s concealment and investigation.

subject: Candlekeep Apothecary
fact: The apothecary is the suspected source of the poison; its pet squirrel, communicable by Daz, may hold vital clues about the poison’s origin or delivery method.

subject: Janussi's Office
fact: Janussi's office contained the wrapping paper from his Secret Santa gift, contradicting its expected location and suggesting tampering or misdirection after the murder.

subject: Deadwinter Night
fact: The murder occurred on the night of the Deadwinter supper, a traditional Candlekeep holiday marked by feasting, gift-giving, and ritual — a time of distraction exploited by the killer.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is an ooze entity with no natural senses, who attempts to assist through adaptive physical changes; despite lacking eyes, nose, or ears, it persists in seeking utility — a non-human intelligence struggling to comprehend human needs.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is the investigator who uncovered the heart and cleaver in the Milil chalice, deduced the lead-lined concealment, and conducted interviews with junior avowed witnesses; he operates on blunt logic and physical evidence.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was the poison taster at the feast and died at midnight, her death initially treated as collateral damage with no connection drawn to the primary victim.
source_quote: If the only mark was Janussi, the taster's just collateral: she tastes the poisoned dish, she's dead at midnight too.

subject: Sprig
fact: Sprig volunteered to taste every dish at the feast despite being told it was unnecessary, demonstrating initiative that drew attention and suspicion.
source_quote: She insisted. The chefs told her it wasn't necessary. She insisted.

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas, a tiefling, was seen searching the kitchens by candlelight at 1 a.m., pointing to her throat to indicate she was hoarse, and was helped by Sprig to find honey.
source_quote: She ran into Sylvira Savikas searching by candlelight... the tiefling just pointed at her throat, too hoarse to talk.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist was observed feeding a scrap of paper to a candle flame, then dropping it when two junior avowed entered, raising suspicion about hidden communications.
source_quote: Alkrist had been holding a small scrap of paper toward a candle, feeding it to the flame, and when two junior avowed walked in, he dropped it.

subject: Orrin Glass
fact: Orrin Glass, a deaf waiter with keen observational skills, reported that the string around Janussi’s gift had been cut and retied — a critical clue indicating internal tampering.
source_quote: The string tied around Janussi's Deadwinter gift had clearly been cut and retied.

subject: A'lai Aivenmore
fact: A'lai, a dark-skinned elf, visited the apothecary requesting fennel for indigestion and was led by Leuwin to the greenhouse, creating an alibi during the toxin theft.
source_quote: At three, A'lai arrived asking for fennel for indigestion, and Leuwin took him down through the rear exit to the greenhouse below.

subject: Fheminor Scrivenbark
fact: Fheminor, a gnome, visited the apothecary earlier in the day for cold medicine, and was later identified by a squirrel as an unpleasant presence who may have been part of the distraction.
source_quote: He saw the unfriendly girl gnome. Fheminor. Unpleasant, always unpleasant.

subject: Dragonborn
fact: A dragonborn entered the apothecary while Leuwin was occupied, broke a vial labeled 'Dangerous Toxins,' and stole the poison — acting as the physical agent of the crime.
source_quote: A huge lizard skin came in and made a big mess... Something went *bling* and shuddered, and the lizard moved things around, and then left.

subject: Drow
fact: A drow bribed a squirrel with acorns to gather information, and orchestrated the diversion by distracting Leuwin, ensuring their hands remained clean of the poison.
source_quote: A drow on his knees, bribing a squirrel one nut at a time.

subject: Candlekeep Chefs
fact: The Candlekeep chefs were unaware that Sprig had volunteered to taste every dish, and explicitly told her it was unnecessary — indicating a gap in protocol.
source_quote: The chefs told her it wasn't necessary. She insisted.

subject: Great Readers
fact: The Great Readers were involved in a power struggle, with Teles Ahvoste making advances toward Irony and Alkrist being a new, poorly understood entrant to the group.
source_quote: Teles Ahvoste... making passes at Irony... Alkrist, the new one nobody could tell me much about.

subject: Poisoning at the Feast
fact: A poison was administered during the feast, killing the primary target, while Janussi, the poison taster, died as an unintended consequence — the two deaths were deliberately unconnected.
source_quote: Nobody ties the two deaths together. The killer loses nothing.

subject: Tampering with Janussi’s Gift
fact: The string around Janussi’s wrapped gift was cut and retied, indicating that the poison was placed in the package after it was originally sealed — a crime committed in the room by someone present.
source_quote: The string tied around Janussi's Deadwinter gift had clearly been cut and retied.

subject: Toxin Theft at the Apothecary
fact: A highly toxic vial labeled 'Dangerous Toxins' was broken and stolen during a coordinated distraction: A'lai was led away to the greenhouse while the dragonborn stole the poison upstairs.
source_quote: Leuwin wasn't in the room... the dragonborn... broke the vial.

subject: Candlekeep Apothecary
fact: The apothecary is a living oak tree with shelves inside its trunk; a vial of dangerous toxin was broken and concealed with a peppermint rag on the top shelf.
source_quote: An actual evergreen oak grown out of the burrows... a peppermint-soaked rag and a broken vial... labeled, in Elvish, *Dangerous Toxins.*

subject: The Non-Christmas Christmas Tree
fact: A tree in the Readers' Tower held wrapped gifts — all books — where the string around Janussi’s gift was tampered with, and where Alkrist was seen burning a scrap of paper.
source_quote: The pile under the — the non-Christmas Christmas Christmas tree... All the gifts were books anyway.

subject: The Greenhouse Below Candlekeep
fact: A magical greenhouse beneath the apothecary was used to grow herbs year-round and served as the alibi location where A'lai was distracted while the poison was stolen upstairs.
source_quote: Leuwin took him down through the rear exit to the greenhouse below, where he grows herbs year-round with magic.

subject: The Cut and Retied String
fact: The string on Janussi’s gift had been cut and retied — a deliberate act proving the poison was inserted after the gift was wrapped, implicating someone present at the event.
source_quote: The string tied around Janussi's Deadwinter gift had clearly been cut and retied.

subject: The Dead Rats in Alkrist’s Chamber
fact: Alkrist kept sealed jars of dead rats with blistered, pustule-covered skin — evidence he was studying the effects of poison on living tissue.
source_quote: Sealed glass jars holding dead rats, their skin blistered and risen into pustules.

subject: 1001 Tashalian Nights
fact: Alkrist’s copy of *1001 Tashalian Nights* had a bookmark on the tale of a commander poisoned by a magic horn coated in Midnight Tears — a direct parallel to the current crime.
source_quote: The bookmark sat on the tale of a military commander, poisoned by a gift of surrender — a magic horn whose mouthpiece had been coated in Midnight Tears.

subject: The Honey Pot
fact: A pot of honey was found in the kitchens and given to Sylvira Savikas — potentially a cover for her inability to speak, or a prop to mask her true condition.
source_quote: Sprig helped her find a pot of honey and said goodnight.

subject: Irony’s Silence
fact: Irony, who cannot lie, deliberately steered the investigation toward Sprig instead of answering questions directly — a calculated evasion that suggests hidden knowledge.
source_quote: She hadn't answered. She'd pointed us at Sprig instead. Can't lie isn't has to tell.

subject: The Drow’s Role
fact: A drow bribed a squirrel to gather intelligence but never touched the poison — a masterful act of deniability that makes them the likely architect of the plot.
source_quote: The drow caused the diversion and kept his hands clean of the highly toxic poisons.

subject: The Dragonborn’s Motive
fact: The dragonborn physically stole the poison but left no known motive — their identity and reason for acting remain unknown, making them the most dangerous variable.
source_quote: The dragonborn did the upstairs work and the handling of a substance that might kill you.

subject: The Squirrel’s Testimony
fact: The squirrel, Nibbles, provided key testimony about the apothecary theft, but was paid with nuts — raising questions about the reliability and completeness of its account.
source_quote: Nibbles loved nuts. I had nuts. We understood each other immediately.

subject: The Book as Weapon
fact: The poison was delivered via a wrapped book — the same medium used in the tale Alkrist was reading — suggesting the killer intended to mirror the literary method of murder.
source_quote: The book sitting wrapped in that package... the tale of a military commander, poisoned by a gift of surrender — a magic horn... Midnight Tears.

subject: 1 a.m. — Kitchens Encounter
fact: Sylvira Savikas was seen in the kitchens at 1 a.m., searching by candlelight and unable to speak — a critical anomaly in the timeline of the investigation.
source_quote: One in the morning.

subject: Midnight — Deaths
fact: Both the primary victim and Janussi died at midnight, confirming the poison had a delayed effect — likely activated by ingestion at the feast.
source_quote: She's dead at midnight too.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool, a sentient ooze, was used by Zalthir to infiltrate and search the Readers' chambers, flowing where Zalthir could not and reading what Zalthir could not understand.
source_quote: The ooze had come out of the bag eager... He flowed where I could not reach; I read what he could not understand.

subject: Nibbles (Squirrel)
fact: Nibbles, a squirrel, acted as a witness to the apothecary theft after being bribed with acorns — a non-human informant whose testimony revealed the division of labor between the drow and dragonborn.
source_quote: A drow on his knees, bribing a squirrel one nut at a time.

subject: Leuwin
fact: Leuwin, the satyr apothecary, was distracted by A'lai’s visit to the greenhouse and was unaware the toxin was stolen during his absence.
source_quote: Leuwin wasn't in the room... he couldn't imagine how it had happened.

subject: Teles Ahvoste
fact: Teles Ahvoste, a Great Reader, made persistent romantic advances toward Irony, possibly creating motive for sabotage or retaliation.
source_quote: Teles Ahvoste... making passes at Irony.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir, a searcher of the Readers' chambers, used Glabbagool to investigate the suspects, and discovered Alkrist’s study of poison and his bookmarked tale of literary poisoning.
source_quote: I read the man as much as the book... The bookmark sat on the tale of a military commander, poisoned by a gift of surrender.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral, a suspect in the investigation, was noted to be terrified and overly eager to help — likely a red herring, as he was poisoned himself and thus not the killer.
source_quote: The man was scared out of his skin, kept eyeing Dawnbringer like he wanted to kiss the blade's feet and beg it off him.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm, one of the Great Readers, was eager to fire the old boss and seat a new one — indicating a power motive within the leadership struggle.
source_quote: Bookwyrm, eager to fire the old boss and seat a new one.

subject: Kazryn Nyantani (Tani)
fact: Kazryn Nyantani, the chief cleric, was among the eight named suspects in the investigation, though no specific evidence was tied to them yet.
source_quote: And Kazryn Nyantani — Tani — the chief cleric.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz would note the locked safe without regret, as we are not the famed Whistler, no safecracker of that old generation among us.
source_quote: Daz would note it without regret: we are not the famed Whistler, no safecracker of that old generation among us.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool could not thin himself past the one-finger-width opening of the safe, and left it sealed to keep its secret.
source_quote: Glabbagool could not thin himself past it. We left the safe to keep its secret.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm's chambers took half the top floor — comfortable, neatly arranged, no extravagance — and she entered, found nothing, and tasted the air, finding no poison.
source_quote: Bookwyrm last, and by then the tower was fighting me. Her chambers took half the top floor — comfortable, neatly arranged, no extravagance to it. I got in. I found nothing. Glabbagool tasted the air and found no poison in it.

subject: Midnight Tears
fact: The name 'Midnight Tears' was kept where it would not be lost, as a significant lead.
source_quote: Midnight Tears. I kept the name where I would not lose it.

subject: cage missing birds
fact: A cage is missing three birds, contributing to the cluster of leads.
source_quote: A cage missing three birds.

subject: jars of blistered rats
fact: Jars of blistered rats were found, contributing to the cluster of leads.
source_quote: Jars of blistered rats.

subject: page marked to poisoning by gift
fact: A page was marked to a poisoning by gift, contributing to the cluster of leads.
source_quote: A page marked to a poisoning by gift.

subject: clean room
fact: The room was clean and free of poison, and that absence was noted as information.
source_quote: A clean room. That, too, was information.

subject: we had several leads
fact: Multiple leads were identified: missing birds, blistered rats, a marked page, and a clean room.
source_quote: We had several. A cage missing three birds. Jars of blistered rats. A page marked to a poisoning by gift.
